A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Zephyrus, ZephyrusWorld, and ZephyrusBench. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching renumbered tasks and relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations of Direct, Reflective, and text-only systems using four LLM backbones, with aggregate and task-level results in Section 5 and Appendices A.4–A.6.

after.justification: V2 reports original evaluations using five LLM backbones, plus tool ablations, a ground-truth forecaster comparison, failure analysis, and repeated-run results in Appendix A.4.

M1.justification: V2 adds a Climatology tool providing historical summary statistics across multiple timescales and increases Direct's error-correction limit from 5 to 20 attempts. The core Direct and Reflective workflows remain intact. The JAX-GCM/JCM naming change retains the same described simulator configuration and does not establish a simulator redesign.

E1.justification: Table 2 adds explicit standard-deviation and percentile anomaly queries, an exceedance query, and targeted disaster localization, corresponding to v2 tasks 6, 7, 10, and 48. These extend existing anomaly and disaster task families within the same meteorological data sources; most earlier tasks remain under different numbers.

E2.justification: The main comparisons remove GPT-5-Nano and add GPT-5.2 and Qwen3-30B, including their evaluated text-only baselines. Appendix A.4 additionally evaluates a Geolocator-and-Climatology-only baseline and a ground-truth forecaster comparator. These introduce substantive information-access controls beyond v1's text-only, Direct, and Reflective comparisons.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation changes from LLM validity checking followed by extraction to structured extraction followed by programmatic validation and up to three extraction retries. Direct's execution budget increases from 5 to 20 attempts, and benchmark composition changes from 2,158 to 2,230 samples. V2 also revises some synthetic-task thresholds, adds IoU reporting, and introduces tool-removal and ground-truth forecasting protocols on 50% subsamples.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's difficulty and task breakdowns, v2 adds a four-turn storm-detection failure case, tool-use and runtime-error analysis, leave-one-tool-out ablations, a climatology-only control, and a ground-truth forecaster experiment. Appendices A.4.1–A.4.5 substantially expand evidence about component utility, tool selection, failure causes, and stability.

E5.justification: V1 reports error quantiles but no repeated-run variability. V2's Appendix A.4.5 and Table 8 report three identical-setting runs of Reflective with gpt-oss-120b on a 50% subsample, including per-run values and means with standard deviations. Numerical task tables also add error-standard-deviation columns. Cross-run uncertainty reporting remains limited to one configuration.

E6.justification: Results are broadly revised and expanded. Figure 4 changes GPT-5-Mini's Reflective/Direct/text-only correctness from 54.7/48.5/19.9% to 61.2/58.5/17.0%; Gemini's Direct-versus-Reflective ranking reverses. V2 adds ablation outcomes, human-versus-synthetic breakdowns, and previously unreported per-template results. These are results under revised benchmark and experimental conditions, not controlled same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The discussion-score precision, recall, and F1 definitions and the task-correctness formulas and thresholds are retained. Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs. V2's additional empirical metrics and reformatted equations do not introduce new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The environment, agent-family, and benchmark contributions remain central. V2 adds climatology to the stated environment contribution, updates the headline advantage from up to 35 to 44 percentage points, and replaces the claim of hard-task parity with text-only baselines with the broader statement that hard tasks remain challenging even for frontier LLMs.

C2.justification: V2 develops specific explanations beyond v1's general discussion of difficult meteorological reasoning: fixation on the deepest global pressure minimum, inappropriate simulator use for short-term forecasting, and failure to invoke the simulator for counterfactuals. It interprets the ground-truth forecaster experiment as showing that accurate forecasts alone do not resolve hard-task reasoning and domain-knowledge limitations.

D1.justification: V2 adds code and benchmark access information, the text-only baseline prompt, the generation model and source-report details, and the high reasoning-effort setting. It documents the climatology reference period and aggregation timescales. These are useful disclosures, although the retained Direct and Reflective prompt listings still omit the new climatology argument.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations for JCM, Gemini 2.5, the gpt-oss model card, MathVista, and MMMU. It explicitly attributes the simulator to JCM and supports the discussion of quantitative VLM weaknesses with additional references. The broader positioning relative to scientific agents, weather models, and multimodal weather datasets remains stable.

P1.justification: V2 makes targeted edits to the abstract, evaluation description, results, and conclusion, reorders related-work paragraphs, and adds a Section 5.1 guide to supplementary analyses. The appendix moves prompts from A.7 to A.3 and groups results beneath A.4. Much of the original introduction, method exposition, and task descriptions remains unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adopts conference formatting, redraws the framework diagrams, restyles the performance plots, and combines the three difficulty plots into one figure. It adds failure-case and tool-use figures, ablation and variance tables, separate human/synthetic result displays, and extensively expanded per-task tables with additional metric columns. These are substantial visual and structural changes beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: V1 mainly established benchmark performance without directly testing tool contributions or explaining failures. V2 substantially addresses that deficiency through tool ablations, a ground-truth forecaster comparison, execution traces, and a repeated-run check. Expanded task-level reporting and access information also improve scrutiny and reproducibility. The narrow scope of the variance study and outdated agent prompt listings remain limitations, but the added diagnostic evidence substantially strengthens the paper's scientific support.
